title: Capacity rotation, surge pool, and prioritized scope-pruning playbook
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Problem: As usage grows and Dedicated commitments increase, we've had ad-hoc mid-cycle scope cuts and last-minute staffing shifts that cause churn. We need a repeatable playbook for (1) allocating a cross-functional surge pool, (2) rotating responsibility for mid-cycle triage, and (3) an explicit, prioritized scope-pruning decision matrix tied to OKRs so teams can make fast, defensible cuts with minimal org disruption.

Goal: Deliver a documented, lightweight process that product, engineering and design leads can follow during cycle planning and mid-cycle emergencies. Reduce unplanned scope slippage by 40% and reduce time-to-decision on scope cuts to under 48 hours.

What this ticket contains: a) operational rules for a 10% surge pool (headcount points) and how to request it; b) a weekly capacity rotation schedule for on-call triage of critical path items; c) a 4-step scope-pruning decision matrix mapped to OKR priority and customer impact; d) templates (request form, approval checklist) and dashboards to track usage; e) rollout and success metrics.

Key proposals (high level):
- Surge pool: reserve ~10% of cycle capacity as an elastic pool that can be borrowed by initiatives with validated customer impact. Borrowing requires a 2-step approval (PM + ENG lead) and a compensating plan for the donor team. Pool is replenished at next cycle planning or via retro-approved top-ups.
- Capacity rotation: 1 engineer and 1 PM from each product squad rotate weekly into a "Critical Path" lane. Their duty is to operate as the rapid decision nucleus for urgent triage, fielding surge requests, and coordinating quick swaps. Rotation schedule maintained in shared calendar and synced to Redwood Console incident channels.
- Scope-pruning matrix: Four attributes scored 0-3: OKR alignment, customer impact, effort remaining, and unblockability (external dependencies). Pre-defined cut thresholds determine low/medium/high candidates for pruning.
- Guardrails: No more than 30% of any squad's committed points may be reallocated without exec sign-off. Critical security or compliance work cannot be pruned.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook doc in Confluence with examples and templates linked.
- Request form (Google Form) and approval flow documented with GitHub issue template.
- Dashboard in Console showing surge pool balance, active borrowings, and rotation calendar.
- Trial run during 2025-W08 with at least 3 borrowing events and a retrospective.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Teams may game the system by over-prioritizing items to access surge pool. Mitigation: require an evidence artifact (customer ticket count, revenue impact, SLA breach) and post-event audit.
- Risk: Rotation increases context switching. Mitigation: cap rotation duty to 8 hours/week and provide compensatory capacity in next planning cycle.

- Request form prototype: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1x-Example
- GH template (PRD+approval): https://github.com/redwood-inference/playbooks/pull/126

2) Incorporate Design input on comms and calendar UX (DES review by 2025-02-20).
3) Finalize approval flow + automation (ticket ENG-20578) and implement dashboard instrumentation.
4) Run trial in 2025-W08 and capture metrics.
